item.content:encoded: I had upvoted this but after learning of the size 0 text I had to downvote. Size 0 text is a cheap gimmick that nobody should use. I won't go around checking every source text to see if the author got cheeky. It doesn't help at all that the hidden text is the most cartoon villainy piece of writing I have seen in months. You can certainly do better.

item.content:encoded: I know this is a Necro, but I'm seconding this. Yes, the 0 text added a bit of depth to the interview and what happened to the MTF, however there is no indication that it exists in the article. You could call it an Easter Egg, you could call it an unnecessary bit for those who can find it. But I didn't even know the 0 text existed until I saw the above comment. There should at least be come kind of clue. Suspicious spacing, an extra bit that gets highlighted when you click and drag, or something.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Dr. L████ N█████

I'm going to hammer on this point repeatedly until this stops showing up. Why would you redact something like this? Are we cleared to know the doctor's name? If not, just strike it entirely. Why would you provide a hint like this if we're not to know this person's identity? What is the purpose of narrowing someone's search to "People with the initials L.N." from "every possible Foundation employee?" This isn't the reason I downvoted, but the sheer pointlessness of this device is immersion-breaking for me.

As to the interview, I'm not sure there's really enough here for a standalone document. It provides some background info, and perhaps because of that it comes across as pretty directly expository. That's kind of an inherent problem with the interview format, I know. There's some lines that sound a little wrong, like they wouldn't be things that come out in natural conversation. "What are you going to do, vivisect me? That would be ironic, wouldn't it? You cutting me up?", "We thought we could stop the bodies falling into our world", these sorts of things. The whole exchange could use a once-over to check for how this would sound as an actual conversation.

As to the size-zero text, I didn't bother. That's a gimmick that I don't see the point of, and I've never felt it's incumbent on me as a reader to go digging through source code to find things that are integral to enjoyment of the piece. If the writer is making it actively harder for the reader to read the piece, then I'm inclined to say that the writer is not doing their job.
